body:
The 2026 World Series shifts to St. Petersburg as the Milwaukee Brewers look to take a dominant 3-0 series lead over the Tampa Bay Rays. The Rays, meanwhile, are trying to get on the board in Game 3 behind Freddy Peralta at home at Tropicana Field.No team has erased a 2-0 deficit in the World Series since the 1996 New York Yankees.The Rays secured the American League pennant by beating the Cleveland Guardians in ALCS Game 6 behind a massive home run by Junior Caminero. This marks their first World Series appearance since 2020, and only their third in franchise history (they lost to the Philadelphia Phillies in 2008). The Brewers, meanwhile, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to win the National League pennant and make their first World Series since 1982. Neither franchise has ever won a title, meaning we'll get a first-time champion regardless of the outcome.

title: What Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace injuries mean for the Thunder and why a trade isn't so simple - CBS Sports
description: There was something poetic about the way Jalen Williams opened the 2026-27 season. His numbers only jumped off the page if you were look
body:
There was something poetic about the way Jalen Williams opened the 2026-27 season. His numbers only jumped off the page if you were looking for symbolism. He scored 12 points, the same margin by which the Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the San Antonio Spurs. The message, if you believe in such things, was pretty clear: after losing to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals largely without him a year ago, Jalen Williams is the player that pushes the Thunder over the top against their nemesis. He is the difference between another parade and another defeat.And now, his season is likely over. On Sunday, in a game against the very Los Angeles Clippers whose 2022 first-round pick brought Williams to Oklahoma City in the first place, the Thunder star suffered what appeared to be a devastating ankle injury on an attempted dunk. Now we have a diagnosis: a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula. He will have surgery and be sidelined for at least several months and potentially the whole season.To make matters worse, starting shooting guard Cason Wallace has a torn labrum in his left shoulder. His outlook is similar to Williams': surgery, an extended absence, and possibly a lost season.For most teams, losses like this could be season-ending. The Thunder are not most teams. They made it to Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals without Williams a year ago. Losing Wallace as well further complicates matters. The Thunder still have the MVP. They still have depth and an almost infallible infrastructure for regular-season winning.
But they've certainly ceded their place as championship favorites, so where does Oklahoma City go from here? Where would a Williams and Wallace-less version of the Thunder stand in a crowded championship picture? What can they do to improve in their absence? And what does all of this mean for Oklahoma City's longer-term plans? Let's attempt to answer these questions as the Thunder prepare to move forward without one of their best players.What does this mean for the Western Conference pecking order?The Thunder went 39-10 without Williams a year ago. That's a 65-win pace. Their +10.9 net rating in the minutes spent without him would tie for the 16th-best full-season figure in NBA history. They used only four Williams-free lineups for at least 50 minutes a season ago, but all four of them outscored opponents by at least 18.6 points per 100 possessions. The situation is obviously more dire with Wallace hurt as well, but it goes to show how resilient this organization is. The Thunder are used to winning shorthanded. This is a regular-season wins machine that will earn a high seed so long as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander stays relatively healthy. Of course, the Thunder don't judge themselves by regular-season performance. The measuring stick is, of course, San Antonio.
Victor Wembanyama disarms Gilgeous-Alexander in ways no other defender can by taking away the basket completely. He made a league-best 6.6 field goals per games off of drives last season. That figure was nearly cut in half in the Western Conference Finals. Gilgeous-Alexander isn't much of a pull-up 3-point shooter. Without anyone to take pressure off of him, he was reduced mostly to contested, mid-range jumpers by the end of that series. He nearly made enough of them to win it in Game 7. That still isn't a viable recipe against a Spurs team that figures to be even more imposing with a full playoff run under its belt.Ajay Mitchell missed most of that series too. If he's healthy this time around, if Jared McCain takes the step that his early performance suggests that he could, if Chet Holmgren doesn't turn into a pumpkin again next May, if Wallace can at least make it back and play in a smaller role, and if San Antonio deals with a health issue or two of its own, then maybe the Thunder can still climb Mount Victor. The odds will be stacked against them on that front, and the road to that matchup is more treacherous than ever.The Los Angeles Lakers, Houston Rockets and Minnesota Timberwolves are all undefeated thus far. The Denver Nuggets have only lost to the Thunder (though maybe don't look too closely at their only other outing). All four of those teams were badly banged up last spring. Inevitably, one or two of them will be again this year. Someone in that group will be healthy enough to pose a threat. The Thunder know from experience how terrifying Luka Dončić and Nikola Jokić can be in a seven-game setting. Williams is their best defender by far for the former and a necessary athletic counter for the latter. Wallace's defense would be vital against Minnesota's star guard tandem. Their absences erase Oklahoma City's absurd talent advantage over the field. Without them, the Thunder are distressingly mortal.
The field knows that. The Rockets, given their deep pool of assets, are uniquely qualified to go for it. We came into the season expecting a two-team race out West. Now, we're one Spurs injury away from a wide-open field. One or two of those second-tier contenders will make a win-now push. The Thunder are vulnerable this year. They may not be next year. The time to get them is here and now.That window extends to the regular season. The Spurs aren't exactly optimizing for regular-season wins right now, instead choosing to settle their starting lineup debate now so it's not a concern in June. The De'Aaron Fox-Stephon Castle-Dylan Harper trio is struggling offensively thus far. The Spurs will course-correct eventually and win a bunch of games. But suddenly, home-court advantage in the West seems gettable. This iteration of the Thunder has never started a playoff series on the road.Oklahoma City's margin for error has mostly evaporated. Remember, the Thunder traded Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to duck the second apron. They came into the season as the NBA's deepest team, but that depth is no longer a superpower. It's only October. Other players will inevitably get hurt. Losing Williams may not end Oklahoma City's season, but every subsequent injury hurts that much more without him to cover their gaps. Reinforcements of some sort are probably a necessity.
Can Oklahoma City replace Williams on the trade market?Sam Presti was asked about a possible trade at his press conference Monday. He offered little insight. "For me, the last 24 hours or whatever it's been is all about people," Presti said. "I know you have to ask the question. ... I haven't really given a lot of thought to that. Right now, it's about those two guys and their families and trying to be there for everybody, working through all the medical information." In reality, he doesn't know the answer yet. Almost one-third of the league is not currently tradable because of contractual restrictions that lift in December and January. That should suit Oklahoma City fine. The Thunder need time to see where they stand.A minor moment from the offseason looms large right now. While the Denver Nuggets were locked in a restricted free agent standoff with Peyton Watson, the Thunder attempted to swoop in and steal Spencer Jones on an offer sheet that pushed the Nuggets into the second apron. Denver matched. The Thunder retained their $7 million or so in second apron room... but couldn't swipe the defensive forward they had hoped would replace Dort. As good as Oklahoma City's perimeter defenders are, they're mostly small. Size was already a priority.That sort of archetype may be a target again. Ideally, it would be someone in that price range, $7-10 million, so the Thunder can remain below the second apron for at least this season. Derrick Jones Jr. is a sensible name on this front, and so is Herb Jones now that the New Orleans Pelicans have bizarrely cut his playing time. Others will come up closer to the deadline.
The Thunder can get a bit more ambitious if they want. They have a $17.7 million trade exception, offering them a bit of room to bring in a decent-sized salary. If they want to replace some of Williams' offense, Rui Hachimura or Max Strus would fit into that exception, though the Thunder would have to offload salary elsewhere to get back below the second apron.A year ago, the Thunder stole McCain through pure opportunism. There was a player on another team they liked with several years of cheap team control remaining and a roster that no longer fit him. They swooped in with a first-round pick they could afford to trade. Most contenders don't have those lying around. The Thunder still do, if there's a similarly affordable young forward out there they like. Those are harder to find than guards. Here's a name: Jaime Jaquez. The Milwaukee Bucks didn't sign him to a rookie extension, and the Thunder couldn't afford to keep him in restricted free agency. But he'd give Oklahoma City badly needed ball-handling depth and size, and he's the sort of high-IQ player they tend to prize.The guard market, should the Thunder instead prioritize a Wallace replacement, is usually a bit deeper. If Orlando determines it cannot afford to re-sign Anthony Black in restricted free agency, for instance, the Magic are asset-poor enough to consider a deal at the deadline. The Thunder have even greater long-term affordability questions than the Magic do, but have far more reason to invest in this season than Orlando. A short-term addition makes sense if it preserves a championship window.
There are going to be calls for something more substantial. The Thunder have all of the draft picks in the world! Why can't they just trade a handful of them for another star? That's easier said than done for a few reasons.Oklahoma City's draft surplus is smaller than you think and mostly evaporates after its three first-round picks in the weak 2027 class. After 2027, their only external first-round picks are a 2028 swap with the Dallas Mavericks and a top-5 protected pick from Denver in 2029. They still have their own picks, and they still have more than almost everyone else. But it's not 2021 anymore. They don't control Clipper picks from here until eternity.The Thunder have way less matching salary than they used to. If this had happened a year ago, the Thunder could've used the Dort, Joe and Wiggins contracts to pivot into a bigger name. They didn't at least in part because they expected Williams to be ready by the postseason. Well, they may not this time around, but they don't have those contracts lying around anymore either. They have three max players (Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Holmgren), two essential, veteran role players (Isaiah Hartenstein and Alex Caruso), and then everyone else makes less than $8 million. Now, some of the players in that bottom tier are pretty straightforward contract fodder (Nikola Topić, Thomas Sorber and Kenrich Williams get you to $15 million in flotsam quickly and harmlessly), but that's not close to a star's salary.The Thunder can aggregate salaries, but only if they stay below the second apron in doing so. If they take back more money than they receive in a trade, they create a first-apron hard cap they cannot abide.Imagine a player like Trey Murphy. He's on a contract widely believed to be team-friendly. He plays the same position as Williams, and while he's nowhere near his equal defensively, he could adequately replace him on offense. He's been in trade rumors for years. Nobody has met New Orleans' asking price, but the Pelicans haven't negotiated with a team as asset-rich as the Thunder. If the cost is three first-round picks, the Thunder could do that.But Murphy makes $27 million, and the Thunder couldn't functionally match that figure without including Alex Caruso. Depriving this defense of Caruso, with Dort gone and Williams and Wallace hurt, weakens it in ways the Thunder would surely deem unacceptable. In the 2023 CBA, making the money work for a trade like this is often harder than stacking the assets.
All of this essentially means that if the Thunder want to add a star-level player, he would have to be making a preposterously low salary. Such players technically exist, but they're typically not available for trade. Could the Thunder go to, say, the Portland Trail Blazers and offer them five first-round picks for Deni Avdija? Sure. Avdija is making less than $14 million this season, and he's roughly on Williams' tier as a player. But unless Portland's season goes sideways in a way that it hasn't thus far, the Blazers likely aren't interested in giving up Avdija. Ditto the similarly underpaid Nickeil Alexander-Walker in Atlanta. Contracts like this are rarely traded.If the Thunder identify a gettable player of that ilk? By all means, go for it. Their draft pick surplus represents helpful liquidity on that front. The Thunder could theoretically make a substantial draft pick investment in the right player without fear of long-term repercussions because they could simply flip that player elsewhere in the offseason to get most of those picks back once Williams comes back. They're so loaded long-term that they could effectively rent someone for this year's title push if they wanted to. Most teams couldn't afford the inherent risk of doing so because they only have their own picks -- and the access to rebuilding those picks offer -- to trade. The Thunder obviously don't have such concerns. That's the benefit of managing an external surplus.Still, the reality of a star-level acquisition is that the Thunder would probably have to send a star-level salary out in order to make one. Gilgeous-Alexander is untouchable, and if the Thunder were going to trade Holmgren it probably would have happened last summer after his meltdown against the Spurs. So... are Williams and Wallace fully off of the table?
What will this mean for Williams and Wallace in the long term?Wallace is the easier answer. The Thunder almost certainly won't trade him. He's on a far more affordable contract than Williams, and that deal is much harder to trade thanks to the poison pill that comes with rookie extensions. Because Wallace signed an extension, his outgoing salary in a trade would be his actual cap number for this season. However, his incoming number for the acquiring team would be the average of his current salary and the salary he'd earn in any subsequent seasons he's under contract. More simply: he'd count for around $7 million in outgoing salary to the Thunder, but around $24 million to a new team. Expect him to stay put.Williams is a bit more complicated. A trade involving him this season, for a multitude of reasons, seems enormously unlikely. Since when do the Thunder ever trade someone from a position of weakness? Considering his recent history of injuries, his trade value is just almost certainly too low to justify giving up a former All-Star in his mid-20s. You're not trading Williams for a bloated contract and one or two picks just to maximize this year's push. Even if that was the proper basketball decision, it would just be so out of character for the Thunder organizationally. This is a team that prizes its culture and developmental infrastructure more than just about any team in the league. Giving up on one of its great success stories after a terrible injury is just callous in a way that the Thunder have never been. This is a notoriously player-friendly organization. These things matter to the Thunder.
And yet, the following facts loom large over the Thunder both now and later:With each passing season, the young Spurs get closer to their primes and the Thunder lose depth to the aprons. You could therefore argue that Oklahoma City's optimal play is to frontload its championship equity, essentially making long-term sacrifices to maximize its chances this year and in the next few. The Thunder tend not to think this way, and the parity era inserts a degree of randomness into these conversations that didn't previously exist in the same way, but if you think the Spurs are headed for a dynastic run, real thought should be given to trying to sneak your championships in now before they peak.Williams played hurt throughout the 2025 playoffs. He barely played in the 2026 playoffs. He may now miss the entire 2027 postseason. These were unrelated injuries to different body parts, and the latest looked more like a fluke than anything. The Thunder know far better than we do how injury-prone Williams will be moving forward. But given how expensive this roster is about to get, the prospect of paying max money to someone you can't rely on to stay healthy is terrifying. Is the hope of keeping Williams healthy worth sacrificing lesser yet healthier players? Again, it's a real conversation. But players like Mitchell and McCain won't be cheap forever. Wallace starts his rookie extension next season.It's easy to forget this considering how accomplished the Thunder are... but this is still a relatively young team. It's still growing. What happens if players grow in ways that make Williams more expendable? What if players thrive without Williams but might be forced into lesser roles upon his return? These are first-world problems, but problems nonetheless. If he's done for the year, Williams will have played just 41 regular-season and playoff games combined last season and this year. The team he returns to next season will be very different from the one he was largely healthy on two years ago. He's a very adaptable player, but integrating someone this significant into a team that has grown used to playing without him poses real questions.Again, the notion of an immediate trade is enormously unlikely. It's exceedingly rare for a team to trade a 25-year-old All-Star who wants to play for them, especially when he already has a championship ring. But Oklahoma City was facing difficult long-term questions already, and this injury only makes things harder. For now, we'll see how the next few months play out. The Thunder won't rush anything. They'll want to know for certain what they have in this roster and what's available to them externally before making any big decisions. But those decisions are coming, and with this season's championship push suddenly weakened, they may be coming sooner than we previously imagined.

title: Who's to blame for Manchester United's decline? Ranking the biggest culprits - CBS Sports
description: It's happened again. Another season, another Manchester United crisis. No longer does the end of daylight savings time herald the harsh
body:
It's happened again. Another season, another Manchester United crisis. No longer does the end of daylight savings time herald the harsh winter ahead. Instead, it is the boos that ring around Old Trafford as the United faithful turn their ire on the same owners, the same executives and the same players, well aware it will be a different coach that pays the price.Sunday's 3-0 defeat to AFC Bournemouth was remarkable only for the sheer unremarkability of it. In the 74 years after their first meeting in the 1949 FA Cup third round, Bournemouth won three games against Manchester United. In the last two years they have won three games: all at Old Trafford, all 3-0. Freddie Kruger is treading the boards at the Theatre of Dreams.Although maybe that analogy is not quite apt. After all, the one positive that you could say about a Krugerian nightmare is that it tends to be a one-and-done situation. No such luck if you happen to be a Manchester United supporter. Could any of them now believe that sacking Michael Carrick would fix anything about this club? They've tried the Eddie Howe-esque Premier League mainstay, the relentless winner a la Antonio Conte, the graduate of the Ralf Rangnick pressing academy in the mold of Julian Nagelsmann. Their shortlist only needs an ex-Ajax coach to sweep the quadrants of post-Sir Alex Ferguson ineptitude. Fred Grim to Manchester United? Well, doesn't that sound about right?This is a club suffering under profound mismanagement, the sort that no one individual can marshal on their own. So there's plenty of blame to spread around. Let's start doing so, in reverse order of course. Gotta keep you on the page as long as we can. Build some suspense. Who might be top, you wonder? Well you probably know. But you know most every AAA movie is going to end with the hero triumphant. The joy is in the journey to the inevitable end point.
5. Michael CarrickNow look, the soon to be former Manchester United manager is not without his faults, as Bruno Fernandes so robustly articulated after the 4-1 defeat in Como. There have been some very weird technical decisions here this season and a head coach with a scintilla of authority probably could have got this team to stop taking so many shots from outside the box. And yet did anyone at Manchester United genuinely think they'd unearthed the next great coach when they threw him the salvage our season post-Ruben Amorim job?
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            That Carrick did so much more than that, guiding United to Champions League qualification through a third-placed finish, spoke to his ability to keep things simple. He retained what had worked from his predecessor, tidied up some of the complexities of the formation and rode Bruno Fernandes' player of the season form as far as he could go. It is not his fault that United have not kicked on since. What had the 45 year old achieved in three seasons at Middlesbrough that suggested a coach who would do much more than what most coaches do, get a team to perform at or around its talent level?Maybe when the stars align, when his team has a game a week and a fully fit squad he could achieve something better than the field but it is no more sensible to project out Carrick's future off the spring hot streak than it is to discount his coaching ability because he has struggled to cope with the first confluence of injuries, unfortunate results and player ill-discipline of his tenure.
Old Trafford seemed to have the right sense of it on Sunday. "It's Carrick you know," reverberated around the ground until the minute he was down the tunnel. Then it was both barrels for everyone else.4. The unbearable weight of being Manchester UnitedNo one associated with Manchester United should apologize for having exacting standards. A well-run version of this club would make every decision based on improving their title-winning prospects either in the short or medium term. There should be no need to take the long way to the Premier League summit.Having said all that, goodness it does not take much to send this club into a doom spiral of nostalgia and despair. When Lisandro Martinez served notice on Jason Wilcox and the hierarchy United had performed pretty well in defeat away to Atletico Madrid, a result that few in the Champions League field could credibly bemoan. Their form had wobbled but only a dodgy Erling Haaland goal had taken Manchester City past them and the last two Premier League results had been disappointing but not disastrous draws.
In short things were not going well but the difficulties were explicable. Up to the loss at the Metropolitano at least one of United's major problems was they had scored fewer goals than their expected goals (xG) for and conceded more than the xG value of their opponents shots. Their actual goal difference was minus-one, their expected goal difference was a shade under plus four. There's some heavy lifting being done in there by thrashing Ipswich Town and Sabah but the aggregate of a good team probably does contain a couple of thrashings as well as games where you play even against seemingly inferior teams like Fulham.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            In short, just as United weren't as good as last season's rise to third place -- the defense started wobbling quite dramatically into the spring -- they aren't really as bad as 16th in the table, a point clear of the relegation zone might have you believe. A clear-eyed assessment both of the relative talent of United and the rest of the league would say that this is a good team vulnerable to a wobble. Just stay the course, keep calm in the dressing room and block out the noise.But, of course... this is Manchester United we're talking about.3. The INEOS sporting hierarchySir Jim Ratcliffe certainly talked a good game when he finally got his hands on the sporting infrastructure at Old Trafford in February 2024, his $1.6 billion investment for around a quarter of the club affording him INEOS Group control of football operations at United. No longer would this be a club in hock to the first team head coach, the Ferguson way of thinking to be replaced by a brain trust that included the sporting director, "probably the recruitment guys" and, for reasons, the chief executive and Ratcliffe himself. "In modern football, you need to decide what's your path and stick to your path," the new minority owner insisted.
In the two and a half years since Manchester United's path has led them to: openly canvass the market for a replacement for manager Erik ten Hag, trigger an extension clause in his contract when they couldn't find anyone better, spend over $400 million outfitting the Dutchman with new players, sack him within four months, hire a coach in Ruben Amorim who had talked himself out of better jobs thanks to his insistence on playing a 3-4-3, finish 15th, sack Amorim just as their analytical profile was on an upswing because he had fallen out with his employers, bring in Carrick temporarily and then permanently, spend almost all their budget on midfielders, get dragged in public by Martinez.That's just the condensed lowlights. It's fair to say that you don't hear much any more about Project 150, the ambitious vision to mark a century and a half of the club with a 21st top flight title. Perhaps by 2028 sporting director Wilcox will have got round to fixing the defense having blown so much of the 2025 summer budget on attack before then spending nearly $200 million on a midfield that needed upgrades but got Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba while the left back spot was left untouched.It would say everything about the cataclysmic mismanagement at a senior level if Wilcox -- like so many at the club a man with little top level experience of the role he has been thrust into -- gets the man said to be his preferred choice to succeed Carrick, Eddie Howe.
The same Eddie Howe who spent a hugely successful two years with Dan Ashworth at Newcastle United. The same Dan Ashworth who Manchester United spent £4.1 million on the poaching of and, five months later, firing of. The same Manchester United who in INEOS' period running the show rank ninth in the Premier League for points, 10th for expected goal difference. Still, at least they sacked staff and cut costs. Who ever could have imagined that as a fix for a business' problems?2. The playersSpeaking after Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, Harry Maguire pulled no punches. "At the moment it's nowhere near good enough and something needs to change," he said. He's not wrong. And yet the only constants at this club sit second and first in our rankings. Cast your mind back to the 4-0 thrashing at the hands of Brentford in August 2022, Erik ten Hag's second game in charge and oh, what, half a dozen crises ago. The starting back four for Manchester United on that Saturday evening in west London? Diego Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw. The starting back four in draws against Fulham and Everton more than four years later? Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw.There are players at this club who have seen off half a dozen permanent managers. Some might not have lasted that long but in their time they have been frozen out or put up for sale. Few have paid the price for inconsistency. Why would you respect the authority of the head coach if you have spent three or four years in the Old Trafford dressing room and seen so many cycle through without any apparent accountability for the playing staff. It seems notable that Cristiano Ronaldo's bombing out by Ten Hag was followed by one of the most impressive runs of results in the last half decade. Players discovered their actions had consequences and started playing like that.
Now, they talk like they are bulletproof. Imagine Martin Odegaard used a post-match interview to mouth off about Mikel Arteta's tactics. Would he ever play for Arsenal again? That's a question Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang can answer. When a player did not perform for Pep Guardiola's Manchester City, he was swiftly sold. Meanwhile United's squad is preserved in aspic. Their defense moves like it is.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            These are not players who lack for talent. United's first choice attack rivals any bar Manchester City and Liverpool. Their midfield needs careful construction to mitigate for its lack of pace but it has quality. When the mood takes them Maguire, Martinez and Shaw are perfectly solid defenders. As the graphic above suggests, this is a team that can have moments of extreme competence. That is how United got to third a few months ago. Were they helped by the coach's tactics or the hierarchy's recruitment? Not really but that does not make these expensive, well-remunerated players innocent bystanders, unable to arrest the decline. 1. The GlazersMore than two decades after Malcolm Glazer loaded debt onto Manchester United to fund his purchase of the club, what has been accomplished beyond a steady degradation of this behemoth of English culture. Being owned by the Glazers, who have not put any money into the club since the takeover, is estimated to have cost the club at least $1.5 billion, much of it spent on servicing debt from the initial takeover. It should be noted that 15 major trophies have been won in the time the Glazers have owned the club but 10 of them came in the period where Ferguson's sheer magnetism held the club together.
There is an argument to be made that United's commercial income skyrocketed under current ownership and certainly this was a club that was among the first to realize that every region could have its own bespoke set of sponsors, that there was always another billboard or patch on the jersey to splash with a logo. Those brands were not, however, flocking to United because of anything the Glazers had done. United were the dominant force in English football at just the right moment to benefit from the Premier League moving from national to global obsession.Far from custodians, the Glazers are the most deleterious of landlords. An extractive force, they provide minimal service and value while taking their management fees, dividends, repayments and then the riches Ratcliffe paid for a slice of the pie. All of their money could have gone into retaining United's preeminence in the English game or at least staving off the impact of their indifference. As if to make the metaphor particularly on the nose, on their watch Old Trafford has decayed such that the cost of renovation, an estimated $1.6 billion, might just make a case for the planned new stadium that no supporter seems to want.A club that even in fallow years ranks among the top 10 revenue generators in football has found itself on a cost-cutting drive for which Ratcliffe is the face both because the Glazers' debt acts as a competitive drag and because ownership showed no interest nor aptitude in improving the on-field product. If the players represent a culture that is accountability-lite then it is ownership that enables it. When we start this piece by warning that nothing will change post-Carrick it is because we have seen enough to know that nothing changes until those who tolerate this degradation of Manchester United are no longer in a position of power.

title: Jalen Williams leg injury: Top-20 NBA star stretchered off court after gruesome fall - CBS Sports
description: Williams was stretchered off the court on Sunday night -- and he's not the only major injury concern for OKC
body:
Williams was stretchered off the court on Sunday night -- and he's not the only major injury concern for OKC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams will need to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle, OKC general manager Sam Presti said Monday. An exact return timeline won't be known until after surgery, Presti said, but ESPN reported that it could be a season-ending injury. Presti disclosed Monday that Thunder guard Cason Wallace will also need surgery. Wallace hurt his shoulder against the Clippers on Sunday and will undergo a procedure to repair a torn labrum. Wallace, too, could be out for the season, per ESPN, but the Thunder had no official timeline on his potential return."Tough night last night. There's no way to paint that differently," Presti told reporters.Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher late in the fourth quarter of a 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night after suffering the severe lower leg injury. With just over a minute to play, Williams drove to the basket and tried to go up for a dunk. He was sandwiched in mid-air by Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr., which caused him to lose his balance. When he landed, his left leg got trapped underneath the weight of his entire body and the lower part of it appeared to break in the wrong direction. 
The Thunder training staff immediately covered his leg with towels as his teammates looked on in distress. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander pulled his own jersey up over his face as Williams' leg was placed into an air cast and he was loaded onto a stretcher. "I just feel bad for him. Nothing more than that," Gilgeous-Alexander said on the court after the win. Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said the team had no immediate update on Williams' status. 
"We're not doing great," Daigneault said. "That's tough on the guys." 
Williams gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was wheeled off the court.Williams was coming off season derailed by injuriesWilliams, 25, emerged as a true star in 2025, when he made his first All-Star appearance and earned a spot on the All-NBA Third Team and the All-Defensive Second Team before helping Gilgeous-Alexander lead the Thunder to their first title since moving to Oklahoma City. Williams averaged 23.6 points in the 2025 Finals and had a playoff-career-high 40 points to lead the Thunder to a Game 5 win that gave them a 3-2 series lead over the Pacers (OKC won in seven games). He played through a wrist injury during the 2025 playoffs, however, and underwent surgery last summer to fix the problem, which kept him sidelined for the first 19 games of last season. Less than two months into his return, he strained his right hamstring and was sidelined for multiple weeks. He came back, played two games, then tweaked his hamstring again and missed another six weeks. Williams returned shortly before the playoffs last season, but suffered a left hamstring strain in Game 2 of the Thunder's first-round series with the Phoenix Suns. He sat out the rest of that series and missed the entire second round before coming back for the Western Conference Finals against the Spurs. After a stellar Game 1, he tweaked his left hamstring again in Game 2 and only played 10 more minutes the rest of the series. 
When the Thunder lost Game 7 to the Spurs, which ended their repeat quest, he was forced to watch from the bench in street clothes. 
        
            
                What Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace injuries mean for the Thunder and why a trade isn't so simple
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Williams and Wallace injuries a major blow to OKC's title chancesThe Thunder made some moves around the margins this offseason -- most notably, trading Lu Dort to the Atlanta Hawks -- but brought back their entire core and hoped to make another run at the title in a top-heavy Western Conference. Vegas oddsmakers installed them as the preseason favorite to win the title, and they started the season with a convincing win over the Spurs. Though he was off to a somewhat slow start, Williams was averaging 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and one steal to begin the season, and was second on the team in scoring behind Gilgeous-Alexander. CBS Sports ranked Williams as the 20th-best player in the NBA in the annual Top 100 player rankings. 
Sunday's win over the Clippers moved the Thunder to 3-0, and even without Dort, they have the depth to withstand Williams' absence -- at least in the regular season. They won 64 games last season largely without Williams. But it will be tougher to withstand Williams' absence with Wallace joining him on the bench.A fourth-year guard, Wallace had worked his way into the OKC starting lineup. He made All-Defense Second Team last season while averaging 8.6 points per game. His emergence was one of the reasons why the Thunder felt comfortable trading away a veteran like Dort. Wallace had started in all three games this season before the injury.Williams' injury draws comparisons to Hayward'sThe gruesome nature of Williams' injury and the reactions it elicited from teammates reminded fans of Gordon Hayward's injury nine years ago.
Hayward, like Williams, dislocated his left ankle and fractured his left tibia on opening night of the 2017-18 season in his debut with the Celtics. He missed the remainder of that season and was never the same player. Hayward appeared in 318 more games over six seasons before retiring at 33 years old.

Philadelphia has averaged just 28.5 rushing yards per game without Barkley, compared with 109.0 yards when he has played

        Week 7 wraps up on Monday night in Philadelphia, as the Eagles host the rival Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles are still without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. However, running back Saquon Barkley will make his return to the field this week, as he's officially active.Barkley was listed as questionable with a hamstring injury prior to Monday night's game. Barkley returned to practice this week, working as a limited participant during Thursday and Friday's sessions. He was even a full participant on Saturday. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards and zero touchdowns in four games this season, but played under 16% of offensive snaps in half of his appearances. He suffered a stinger at the very beginning of Philly's Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans, and then pulled his hamstring in the first quarter of the Eagles' Week 4 meeting with the Los Angeles Rams. It's been a rough season for the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year, but now that he's nearing a return, Barkley could be ready to take off.Eagles with and without Saquon Barkley this seasonWith BarkleyWithout BarkleyW-L2-20-2Rushing yards per game109.028.5Yards per rush4.21.8Barkley averaged 5.1 yards per rush on 36 rushes this season, while all other Eagles running backs averaged 2.8 yards per rush on 71 attempts. The Eagles ran the ball with Dameon Pierce just 12 times last week against the Carolina Panthers, netting 35 yards and a touchdown.
With all of the injuries, this Eagles offense has struggled this season. They have averaged fewer than 4.0 yards per play over three straight games within a season for the first time since 1999, and have been out-gained by 108.3 total yards per game this season, which ranks worst in the NFL. With that said, the Cowboys could be a get-right game for this squad if Barkley is back. The Eagles have won four straight home games vs. the Cowboys, which is tied for the second-longest streak in team history, and have won seven of their past eight primetime games at home.

title: Where to watch Eagles vs. Cowboys: Prediction, odds, TV channel, streaming for 'MNF' - CBS Sports
description: Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts
body:
Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys.Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable. Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite. Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Eagles vs. Cowboys liveDate: Monday, Oct. 26 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: Lincoln Financial Field (Philadelphia)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Cowboys -4.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Cowboys have the ballDallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. (Dak Prescott, typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold. The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys.The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL. Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles.
Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell, Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, among his other targets.The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here.
When the Eagles have the ballThe Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve. Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here.That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold.
Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer.Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr. to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench. If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night. 
PredictionI just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state.Prediction: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20

title: WNBA Finals: Game 6 scheduling debacle an embarrassing end to historic season - CBS Sports
description: What could be the deciding game of the best-of-seven series will now be played as a midweek matinee
body:
What could be the deciding game of the best-of-seven series will now be played as a midweek matinee
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Because time machines are not, in fact, real, there was no perfect solution to the WNBA's Game 6 problem. The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries, tied 2-2 ahead of Game 5 on Monday night at the Chase Center, needed either a schedule change or a location change.And yet, faced with a number of sub-par options, the league delayed the decision until the last possible second, announcing the Game 6 venue just hours before the tipoff of Game 5, and then made the worst choice of the bunch.Game 6 will be played in State Farm Arena at 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, Oct. 29.Yes, that's right. A game during which the champion of the landmark 30th WNBA season could be crowned will take place during lunch on a workday -- and that's for East Coast fans. Valkyries fans, who have shown their second-year expansion team unprecedented levels of support and devotion, will be watching over breakfast, if their jobs and lives and adult responsibilities will permit them to watch at all.To add insult to injury, the game has to be early because there will be a regular-season Atlanta Hawks vs. Cleveland Cavaliers game in State Farm that evening -- the game was shifted from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. to help the arena get turned over in time. But that means that, if a champion is crowned in Game 6, the title-winning celebration and media availability will have to be abruptly cut short in order to accommodate the switch to the men's court. There have even been discussions about moving the on-court celebration to a practice facility, according to ESPN. 
It is simply a baffling decision made inexcusably late in the game, and while I have no doubt that everyone involved will make the most out of it and that the atmosphere at State Farm on Thursday will be as electric as possible given the circumstances, it is an embarrassing subplot to a season that began with the trailblazing new CBA and is ending with two of the best stories in the league -- Angel Reese's emergence with the Dream and the Valkyries' success as an expansion franchise on and off the court -- duking it out in a thrilling best-of-seven series.But hey, nothing puts an exclamation mark on women's sports history like interrupting a championship-clinching, legacy-defining moment so that the men can play a regular-season game.How did we even get here? Well, it's a long story that includes centuries of structural inequities and sexism in sports, but I'll try to keep it to the calendar year. The Dream play their home games at the Gateway Center, a 3,500-seat venue that is the smallest in the WNBA. They began moving marquee games to State Farm Arena, the 17,000-seat home of the Atlanta Hawks, in recent years. This season, thanks in part to the popularity of Reese, who was traded to Atlanta in April, the Dream played five regular-season games in State Farm Arena, and hosted the first two rounds of the playoffs there, too. Next year, State Farm will become the Dream's permanent home.
But when the Dream swept the Liberty to reach the Finals, things got more complicated, primarily because of the start of the NBA season and other scheduling challenges. But all parties came together and figured it out -- Game 3 was moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21 to avoid a Sombr concert, while Game 4 was moved up to 1 p.m. ET to accommodate the Hawks' home opener against the Houston Rockets on Saturday. Both games were sold out and electric. It was understandable that everyone involved wanted to try their best to get Game 6 into that arena as well, and I am extremely sympathetic to the logistical challenges involved with moving NBA and WNBA games, as well as to the financial commitment and risk involved with holding arena space available for games that likely won't even happen.However, none of that excuses the eventual outcome or its timing. The truth is that Dream ownership clearly underestimated the interest in its team off the court and the ceiling of the team on the court, while the WNBA failed to appropriately require contingencies or arrange alternatives themselves once this problem became apparent. And, while moving NBA games to help remedy the situation would have been a nightmare, NBA regular-season games have been moved for many reasons; the league just seemed unwilling to do so in this circumstance.Given all that, the league should have just held Game 6 at Gateway Center at the previously scheduled 8 p.m. time slot and arranged watch parties for Dream fans across the city. 
But by all accounts -- including the public comments of Valkyries owner Joe Lacob after Games 3 and 4 were moved -- the league and the two franchises involved would have found it a bit shameful and optically disadvantageous to hold the Finals in such a small arena. And that's fair; the arena is dark, cramped and very ill-suited for a game that involves this much media coverage and exposure. However, the optics of the move to a matinee game, and the possibility of having a WNBA championship celebration moved because of a far less important men's game, is far worse.The players will roll with the punches, as they always do. In 2018, the Seattle Storm clinched their sweep of the Washington Mystics in the WNBA Finals at EagleBank Arena at George Mason University near Fairfax, Virginia, more than an hour outside of the city, because Capital One Arena was undergoing renovations. The following year, the Mystics won the WNBA Finals in a deciding Game 5 against the Connecticut Sun in their new home arena, a 4,200-seat arena where they still play to this day. Both were far from ideal circumstances, but I covered both in person and the atmospheres were extraordinary. I'm sure Game 6 will be the same.The difference is, in this era, the league and owners have the resources available to do better for the players, the fans and women's sports as a whole. Once again, they chose not to.

title: NFL schedule: League makes rare double flex move by tweaking Week 9 and Week 11 - CBS Sports
description: The NFL just tweaked the schedule for two different weeks in November
body:
The NFL just tweaked the schedule for two different weeks in November
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL rarely announces two weeks' worth of schedule changes at the same time, but that's exactly what the league did Monday. For just the second time this year, the NFL has decided to utilize its flex scheduling powers. This time around, the league is changing the television network for four games while tweaking the kickoff time for one of them. Of the games that were rescheduled, two will kick off in Week 9, while the other two will take place in Week 11. Let's take a look at the changes, starting with the two moves that got made in Week 9. 
WEEK 9 (Nov. 8)Raiders at 49ers, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS)Lions at Dolphins, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on CBS)With this change, the Raiders-49ers game will now be moved into the prime viewing window for Week 9. Fox has the national doubleheader that week, and the network will now have three games to feature in the 4:25 p.m. ET window, with Packers-Patriots and Cardinals-Seahawks also airing on Fox at that time. With 49ers-Raiders moving to Fox, the Texans at Chargers will be the only CBS game in the late window, kicking off at 4:05 p.m. ET. Now, let's check out the changes for Week 11WEEK 11 (Nov. 22)Buccaneers at Lions, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on CBS)Dolphins at Bills, 1 p.m. ET on CBS (Previous: 1 p.m. ET on Fox)The Bills will be moving from Fox to CBS in Week 11, which is certainly the notable news here. Fox actually had a Bills game earlier this season, which is probably one reason this flex went through: the network probably wouldn't have been thrilled to lose that game if it had been its only chance to feature Josh Allen this season. 
With these four flex moves now in the books, there's still one big question to answer in Week 9 and that's whether the NFL ends up flexing the Sunday night game. The Buccaneers are currently scheduled to play in Chicago on Sunday night, but with Tampa Bay sitting at 2-5, the NFL could flex the game. The league has to decide whether to move the kickoff time by the end of the day on Tuesday (Oct. 27). As things currently stand, this is the only Sunday night game on the Bears' schedule, so the NFL might be hesitant to move them out of it. Not to mention, the Bucs have won two of their past three games, so they've certainly looked more competitive over the past few weeks following a 0-4 start. Based on those two facts, it wouldn't be surprising at all if the Buccaneers-Bears end up staying put.

        The moment we've all been waiting for is here: the NFL halftime show performer announcement. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are in charge of selecting the performer, and the rapper has chosen himself.Jay-Z, a New York native, is bringing East Coast hip-hop to the West Coast. The 56-year-old will take the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The stadium is home to the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.The announcement was made across social media with a video. The video was playing "Public Service Announcement" with Jay-Z himself sitting on a stage. 
"From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said, via press release. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."
This marks the first time the rap mogul will perform during the halftime show in any capacity and according to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, it's been years in the making."For several years, we've had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I've seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show," Goodell said. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage."Roc Nation partnered with the NFL in 2019 to produce the halftime show, and since then the 89-time Grammy nominee has been a key decision-maker on who will perform on the biggest stage in football.
The "99 Problems" singer has not announced if he will have any special guests, but since the NFL typically throws in a few surprises for these performances, there is a good chance that pattern will continue. One name that could show up at the Valentine's Day game is Jay-Z's Valentine, Beyoncé. The superstar singer previously performed in two halftime shows. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime once again in her home city, for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyonce Bowl.Beyoncé is no stranger to NFL performances, and considering the two have toured together and have numerous songs, it would make sense.
HOV is currently on the JAŸ-Z30 Tour, celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut studio album "Reasonable Doubt" and the 25th anniversary of "Blueprint." The last time a rapper headlined the halftime show was two years ago when Kendrick Lamar performed and brought out special guest SZA. Other rappers to take the Super Bowl halftime show this decade include Eminem, Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and Lil Jon.The Super Bowl is historically the most-watched game of the year and the halftime show is historically the most-watched performance of the year. Last year, Bad Bunny was the halftime performer. For a look at every Super Bowl performer in NFL history, click here.

        Despite having no coaching experience at any level, former Baylor Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Robert Griffin III would be interested in the Bears' vacancy following Sunday's firing of coach Dave Aranda.Griffin, a college football analyst and Texas native, wants to see his former program nationally relevant again at the highest level."If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor," Griffin said Monday on the Dan Patrick Show. "So yeah, I would 100% be interested. I talked with the athletic director, who is a guy in Doug McNamee that knows what it looks like to win at Baylor, know how you have to win at Baylor and recruit to Baylor to make those things happen."
Griffin set several single-season program records at Baylor in 2011 after throwing for 4,293 yards and 37  touchdowns, to go along with 699 yards rushing and 10 scores. He later earned NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors before injuries derailed a promising career.Since Griffin helped the Bears capture their 10th win in the Alamo Bowl to end this tenure, Baylor has hit 11 or more wins in a single season three times -- including a 12-2 finish in 2021 under Aranda as the Big 12 champions. Only one winning season since fueled Baylor's decision to cut ties with Aranda over the weekend after a loss to Kansas.Griffin mentioned UTSA's Jeff Traylor and Boise State's Spencer Danielson as two coaches he would advocate for the job, along with USC's Lincoln Riley. 
 "I know (Riley's) got his experiences at Oklahoma and obviously, what's going on at USC right now," Griffin said.

Baylor not the only Power Four vacancyPerhaps Griffin stated publicly that he would be interested in Baylor due to the recent development that another Power Four job, NC State, is considering former Wolfpack quarterback and NFL great Philip Rivers for its new head coach.Like Griffin, Rivers is beloved by his former program and enjoyed some of the best seasons in program history during his tenure at NC State in the early 2000s. However, Rivers has coached prep football in Alabama the last six seasons and interviewed in January for the Buffalo Bills' job.
McNamee has been Baylor's new AD for 11 months, and this will mark the first major hire of his tenure. The Bears expect to have a roster capable of competing in the Big 12 next season, including the return of transfer quarterback DJ Lagway in 2027.CBS Sports previously reported the program will likely look for a coach with Texas roots and one who's offensive-minded.

title: More than a championship hangover: Four reasons behind Knicks' troubling 0-3 start - CBS Sports
description: In the entire 80-year history of the NBA, only three champions have started their title defense with an 0-3 start the next season: The 1
body:
In the entire 80-year history of the NBA, only three champions have started their title defense with an 0-3 start the next season: The 1969 Celtics, 2011 Mavericks, and this year's Knicks, who've taken losses to the Sixers, Celtics and, on Sunday night, a Magic team that had also come in winless and was playing without Paolo Banchero.   Last year's title was the product of a legendary postseason run, but this start has provided an opening for all the skeptics to question its sustainability. Were last year's Knicks really that good? They only won 53 regular-season games. They trailed against the Spurs in the Finals for more than 70% of the total minutes played before pulling off multiple basketball miracles.   There was, of course, the largest comeback in Finals history (29 points in Game 4). The OG Anunoby tip-in. The Victor Wembanyama pass off his teammate's back in Game 2. The 16-point rally in the clincher. The Knicks had to overcome a double-digit deficit in every game and Jalen Brunson had to turn into a fourth-quarter folk hero -- which he did, and all credit to him and them, but again, is this a repeatable formula in a much tougher Eastern Conference than the one the Knicks navigated a year ago?  Fair or not, these are the questions this 0-3 start is giving life to. Everyone from Knicks diehards to haters to the few objective ones in between want to know, what's wrong with the Knicks? Was last year a one-year, team-of-destiny wonder, or is this just an early blip on the radar? Let's examine what's behind this 0-3 start.   
  The championship-hangover theory  This is a popular one, but statistically, it holds little water. Of the 26 NBA champions this century, only the 2006-07 Miami Heat won fewer than 51 games in the season following their championship (not counting the strike- and COVID-shortened seasons), and only two -- those same Heat and the 2002-03 Lakers -- have started with a sub-.500 record through the first 20 games.NBA Champion20-game start (following season)Final record (following season)2000 Lakers14-656–26 				 				2001 Lakers17-358–24 				 				2002 Lakers7-1350–32 				 				2003 Spurs10-1057–25 				 				2004 Pistons10-1054–28 				 				2005 Spurs16-463–19 				 				2006 Heat9-1144–38 				 				2007 Spurs17-356–26 				 				2008 Celtics18-262–20 				 				2009 Lakers17-357–25 				 				2010 Lakers14-657–25 				 				2011 Mavericks12-836–30 (Strike shortened)2012 Heat14-666–16 				 				2013 Heat15-554–28 				 				2014 Spurs15-555–27 				 				2015 Warriors20-073–9 				 				2016 Cavaliers13-751–31 				 				2017 Warriors15-558–24 				 				2018 Warriors13-757–25 				 				2019 Raptors15-553–19 				 				2020 Lakers14-642–30 (Covid shortened)2021 Bucks12-851–31 				 				2022 Warriors10-1044–38 				 				2023 Nuggets14-657–25 				 				2024 Celtics16-461–21 				 				2025 Thunder19-164–18 				 				Do the math, and you'll see that defending champions are a combined 366-154 through the first 20 games of the season following their title this century. A 70% win percentage to start the following season with only one sub-51 win team lends zero credibility to the hangover theory. If you're thinking about a repeat, which was already unlikely (it hasn't happened since the 2018 Warriors, it's not looking good. The only team in history to start 0-3 and go on to win the championship that same season is the 1990-91 Chicago Bulls. That's not to say the Knicks can't do it. They defied a lot of historical odds last season, particularly in the Finals. They're going to have to figure this out realtively quickly, though, if they don't want to be digging out of seeding hole the rest of the way. This may not matter much to them as long as they're in the top six, but it should. Again, evidence does not support teams winning titles as anything less than a No. 3 seed. It's only happened two times in history with the 1969 Celtics (No. 4 seed) and 1995 Rockets (No. 6 seed). Knicks fans looking for an excuse will surely cite the distractions of the Karl-Anthony Towns contract debacle and maybe even the James Dolan phishing trip he sprung on his employees as reasons for the slow start. They've played two tough teams in the Sixers and Celtics, and the Magic shot uncharacteristically well from 3. But that doesn't explain New York's own shortcomings in this winless start. So let's address those.Four reasons for Knicks' early season slump1. New York's ice-cold shootingI hate the make-or-miss-league crutch that everyone from coaches to analysts loves to lean on. More times than not, when you're missing shots it's because they're bad shots (either from the wrong people or the wrong spots or they are highly contested adn thus being cause by the defense), and when you're making them it's because they're good shots. That's about process -- ball movement, individual creation, proper spacing, and everything else that goes into sound NBA offense. Still, there is some truth to even good shots simply not going in sometimes, and the bottom line is the Knicks are ice cold to start this season. They have the lowest true-shooting percentage in the league, and only Charlotte has a worse traditional shooting clip than New York's 40.8%. Add in a 32.4% 3-point mark, and you can see why the Knicks own the league's second-worst offensive rating to start the season. This is in stark contrast to the Knicks team we watched buzz-saw its way to the title last season, when they were the playoff leader in both field-goal and 3-point percentage. Think about all the tough shots we watched Jalen Brunson make on that postseason run, particularly late in games. So far, those shots, most of which are pretty similar looks are not going in at anywhere close to the same clip. Other than Towns, who has shot the cover off the ball to start, New York's starters are all struggling to find their early stroke. Brunson, who shot 12 for 28 against the Magic and missed all six of his 3s before finally making one in the final seconds when the game was long over, is at 39% overall and 26% from 3. Anunoby is shooting 41% from the floor and 28% from 3. Josh Hart, who is back to getting the silent treatment as defenses basically don't guard him at the 3-point line to allow for a roaming defender in the paint, is at 41% and 33%, respectively. Every 3-point shot that Hart takes is a win for the defense, and right now he's taking twice as many per game (7.0, up from 3.7 last year) as he has at any point in his career. As stated above, these are the wrong shots. If defenses are going to force Hart into seven 3-pointers each game, the Knicks are going to feel that offensively. And we haven't even gotten to the worst shooter yet ...2. Mikal Bridges has gone from hero to zeroBridges was unquestionably one of the playoff heroes. After a slow start in the first round against Atlanta, he was incredible on both ends throughout New York's run. To say that he's been dreadful to start this season would be putting it politely. Bridges is averaging three points -- 3.3, to be exact -- on 5-for-23 shooting to open the season. He's missed all 10 of his 3-point attempts and, in fact, hasn't made a single jump shot outside the paint. He's got two airballs and has been a shell of his postseason defensive self, and the numbers reflect all of this. So far, the Knicks are registering a minus-26.1 net rating over 183 possessions with Bridges on the floor. Over 109 possessions with him on the bench, that number completely flips to +26.6 with what would rank as the best offense in the league. 
Bridges, whose 10 points are the fewest he has scored over any three-game span since his second year in the league, still has three years and $109 million left on his current deal with a fourth-year player option for another $41.5 million in 2028-29. As the Knicks come into a salary squeeze with Towns, Hart and, eventually, Brunson needing new deals, you have to wonder if Bridges might end up on the trade market if his play doesn't improve considerably. The Knicks likely aren't going to be able to keep everyone if Towns doesn't take a major discount and/or James Dolan backs off his no-second-apron stance. 3. Too many turnoversThe Knicks are turning the ball over on almost 17% of their possessions so far, up from 13.9% last season. That might not sound like a lot (it's about three turnovers per game more), and it's also true that New York turned the basketball over on 16.6% of its possessions in the playoffs and obviously fared more than fine. But it's the points these turnovers are directly leading to for their opponents that are killing them. Through three games, the Knicks are conceding almost 21 points per game off their own turnovers. That's up almost five points from last year's mark, and almost six points from their playoff mark when they were really humming. Against Orlando, the Knicks committed six fourth-quarter turnovers and lost the points-off-turnovers battle 23-12. All told, they are minus-20 in this category for the season. As Mike Brown said following Sunday's loss, "that's a hard gap to make up" when you're not shooting well. 4. Poor transition defenseNew York's lagging transition defense has in part been due to the live-ball turnovers, but they're also just not consistently getting back with enough urgency and shooters are being left open. Late in the second quarter against Orlando, Brunson missed the 3 on one end, then jogged back with his back turned to the play and nobody picked up a knockdown shooter in Desmond Bane, who hit a warmup 3. On the very next possession, Hart turned the ball over at half court and it led to another Bane transition 3. Two mistakes, a seven-point lead became a one-point lead in a matter of seconds. In the opening-night loss, the Knicks gave up 24 fast-break points to the 76ers. According to Tom Haberstroh, that's the most fast-break points the Knicks have conceded in their last 58 games, including the playoffs. 
The Knicks are actually doing a fine job of limiting transition possessions (only the Celtics are operating less in transition as a percentage of their total possessions defended), but when teams have been able to run on them, they have been cut up to the tune of 145.5 points per transition play -- the fourth-worst mark in the league, per Cleaning the Glass. As Brown noted after the Orlando loss, there hasn't been any one factor on which this 0-3 start can be blamed. The Knicks are playing well in stretches and then letting up in others. They gave up 13 fast-break points against the Magic in the first half, cleaned that up to six in the second half, but then committed 11 turnovers. Good shooting can cover for a lot of mistakes in basketball, but right now the Knicks are not shooting well and it's exacerbating all these other parts of the game that they are not executing at a consistent enough level. It's not time to panic, but New York definitely needs to get its act together sooner than later. There is no room for error in this Eastern Conference.
